title: Lightly Steamed Chinese Tofu Dumplings
description: A traditional Chinese dish featuring tender tofu dumplings infused with almond essence, perfect for a cozy meal. This Buddhist-temple-friendly recipe is easy to make and delicious to eat.
instructions: Combine crumbled tofu, almond essence, sesame oil, green onions, garlic, and ginger in a bowl and mix well.
Layout dumpling wrappers on a clean surface and place a small spoonful of the tofu mixture in the center of each wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edge of the wrapper to help seal the dumpling.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point, and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Place the dumplings in a steamer lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between each dumpling.
Steam the dumplings over boiling water for 10 minutes, or until they are cooked through and tender.
Serve the dumplings hot with soy sauce, salt, and pepper to taste.
Garnish with additional green onions if desired.
